PART I

Item 1

ITEM 1. BUSINESS

Management believes we are a technology company whose mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. We develop and support software, services, devices, and solutions.

Our cloud business provides a platform for customers. We continue to invest in artificial intelligence capabilities across our product portfolio. Competition in the technology sector is intense.

Capital expenditure and additions to property and equipment support our datacenter footprint. Management reviews datacenter capacity regularly. We operate datacenters across many regions.

PART I

Item 1A

ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS

Our operations and financial results are subject to various risks and uncertainties.

We face intense competition across all markets for our products and services, which may adversely affect our results of operations.

Management believes our competitors range in size from diversified global companies to small specialized firms. Competition among platform-based ecosystems remains intense and competitors may offer lower prices in every market we serve.

Our focus on cloud-based and AI services presents execution and competitive risks.

We are devoting significant resources to develop and deploy cloud-based and artificial intelligence services. Our competitors are also investing heavily in these areas.

Cyberattacks and security vulnerabilities could lead to reduced revenue, increased costs, and liability claims.

Threat actors, including nation-state actors, continue to target our products, services, devices, and customer data. A cybersecurity incident could result in remediation costs.

We may experience supply or quality problems.

Our devices and datacenter operations depend on components and materials that may be subject to shortages, tariffs, or extended lead times from a limited number of suppliers.

Our business depends on our ability to attract and retain talented employees.

Competition for highly skilled employees remains strong. Changes in headcount, workforce reductions, or severance actions could affect operating expenses.

Laws and regulations relating to the handling of personal data may impede the adoption of our services.

Privacy and data protection regulation continues to expand across jurisdictions and may increase compliance costs.

If our goodwill or amortizable intangible assets become impaired, we may be required to record a significant charge to earnings.

We review goodwill and intangible assets for impairment when events indicate the carrying value may not be recoverable.

PART I

Item 1B

ITEM 1B. UNRESOLVED STAFF COMMENTS

None.

PART II

Item 7

ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

Fiscal Year 2024 Compared with Fiscal Year 2023. Revenue increased driven by growth in our cloud services. Management identified factors affecting gross margin; gross margin percentage decreased slightly driven by scaling our AI infrastructure.

Management noted that cost of revenue increased driven by growth in cloud services and datacenter costs. Operating expenses increased driven by investments in cloud engineering and artificial intelligence.

Capital expenditures, including additions to property and equipment and finance leases, were driven by investments to support cloud demand and our artificial intelligence infrastructure. We expect capital expenditures to increase.

Management reported that cash flow from operations increased driven by higher cash receipts from customers. We returned cash to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases during the period.

PART II

Item 7A

ITEM 7A. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK

We are exposed to foreign currency, interest rate, and equity price risks in the ordinary course of business.
